about: The swimming pool (the other half of sitting 16a) and the Training Yard's evening and night (from sitting 14), written early by hand on 11 Oct 2026, straight after the owner chose the dojo's lit picture (O49): what is left of the Training Grounds.

The pool is composed from words by the four questions of O45, with its view named side by side (Method note 34): seen from its deck looking north along its length, the dojo's white gable end beyond its far end, the roofed gate back to the yard on the left with the yard seen through it, the fence with its lane board and the changing hut on the right, cedars and mountains beyond (mountains are seen to the north only). Its prompt is the tool's `open_yard` sentence, `refs`, the tool's `the_place` sentence with the record's own words for the pool followed by that layout, tools/bgs/stage.txt and look.txt; it passed check_prompts.check for the pool, whose list is the strict one (K16: the word 'bare' is refused there, so the yard's earth is 'sunlit'). Nobody is in the picture.
References: the chosen yard, and a crop of its right side cut from the full-size render (the dojo's wall and gable, and the gate with the pool seen through it).
The yard's two hours are relit from the chosen yard by the tool's own outdoor relight prompt. Its night follows O40 and O44: every window dark, a full moon, nothing added.
refs: Picture 1 is the training yard, already painted: the new picture shows the same school. Picture 2 is cut from the right side of picture 1: the long low hall with its band of windows and its white plastered gable end, and beside it the roofed timber gate, with the pool's water and paving seen through it. The new picture is taken on the far side of that gate, at the pool, looking back towards the school: the hall's gable end and the gate are the same ones, seen from the pool's side. Do not copy the camera or the layout of either picture.

sentences.pool: the school's open-air swimming pool, seen from its timber deck: a pool of twenty-five metres set into a stone terrace on the slope behind a long low hall, edged in the same grey stone as the school's yards, with a low wooden fence, a small changing hut under a grey tiled roof, a lane board on the fence with no lettering, cedars close round it and mountains beyond; the water is still. I stand on the deck at the pool's near end and look along its length towards the school. Across the whole bottom of the picture is the timber deck, level, clear and empty. In the middle, running away from me, is the pool: a long rectangle of clear still water with lane lines painted on its floor, its edges of fitted grey stone. Beyond the pool's far end the stone terrace rises a little, and above it stands the white plastered gable end of the long low hall of picture 2, under its grey tiled roof. On the left, a wide walk of grey stone paving runs beside the pool, with a white plastered wall behind it; in that wall, in the left third of the picture and well short of the far end, stands the roofed timber gate of picture 2, open: this is the way out, and through it I see the sunlit earth of the training yard. On the right, a narrower stone walk and the low wooden fence run beside the pool, the lane board fixed to the fence about halfway along; at the far end of the fence, right of the hall's gable, is the small changing hut. Cedars stand close behind the fence and the hut, and above the hall's roof are more cedars and green mountains under a clear sky. It looks as if it was built with the school, in the same stone, timber and tile, and not added to it
sentences.training_yard_evening: Change the time of day to early evening: a warm orange and pink sunset sky, and low golden sunlight from the left with long soft shadows falling to the right. Everything in the yard and on the hills is still there. Add no new light.
sentences.training_yard_night: Change the time of day to night: a deep blue night sky with stars and a full moon, round and whole, and cool blue moonlight on everything, with soft shadows. Every window of the buildings is dark and no lamp is lit; the water seen through the gate on the right is dark. Everything in the yard and on the hills is still there, as dark shapes against the sky. Add no bench, sign, lamp or light that is not in the picture now.
